 2027 Grammys: Brandi Carlile, Foo Fighters among nominees with WA ties 
 Nov. 16, 2026 at 11:13 am 
 Listen to article 
 Make us a preferred source 
 By 
 Olivia Petty 
 Special to The Seattle Times 
 Washington has plenty of reasons to celebrate heading into Grammy season, but Brandi Carlile is once again leading the local charge. 
 This year has been a big one for Washington’s homegrown folk-rock darling. Between a rip-roaring three-day residency at the Gorge Amphitheatre, a turn on the Super Bowl’s pregame stage and a spot on Time magazine’s 2026 Women of the Year list, Carlile has been on a particularly momentous run with no signs of stopping. Now, she’s picked up four nominations for the 2027 Grammy Awards — taking place on Feb. 7 at Los Angeles’ Crypto.com Arena — all tied to her latest album, “Returning to Myself.” 
 The nominations, announced on Monday morning (full list here ), include best Americana album, a category she’s won twice before, and two nods to the album’s titular song — best American roots song and best Americana performance. Her ballad “You Without Me” rounds out the haul with a nomination for best American roots performance. The Ravensdale-born paragon of alt-country is no stranger to that little golden gramophone, with 11 Grammy wins already on her mantle.  
 As the name suggests, Carlile’s album — her first solo project in more than four years — is an anthemic, inward-looking return to form that comes to grips with the emotional weight of fame and the ways she’s gotten lost in it. A close confidante of musical royalty like Joni Mitchell and Elton John, Carlile wrote the album’s titular song after performing at the massive “Joni Jam” concert at the Hollywood Bowl back in 2024. She said the experience, though abundant, left her feeling spiritually wrung out after years of throwing herself into projects alongside her musical heroes. 
 “Returning to Myself” was an attempt to untether herself professionally from her marquee collaborators and reconnect with her own voice, resulting in a more melodic sound with philosophical lyrical anchors. Through the album, Carlile comes to the conclusion that connection and community are, ultimately, what she loves about music in the first place . 
 Among other groups with Washington ties who’ve received nominations are Seattle-formed heavyweights Foo Fighters, helmed by Dave Grohl, who are up for two categories — best rock album and best rock song — for their 12th studio album, “Your Favorite Toy,” and its title track. The 10-song collection is a short, snappy release featuring the band’s first new drummer, Ilan Rubin, since Taylor Hawkins’ death in 2022. (Their prior release, “But Here We Are,” had Grohl filling in on the kit.) Clocking in at a mere 35 minutes, the album is a full-throttle reminder that Grohl still knows how to rock.
 Advertising 
 Foo Fighters can thank KEXP for some of their competition in the rock brackets. Quebecois art-rock band Angine de Poitrine are also vying for best rock album with “Vol. II,” as well as best performances in rock and alternative music. The masked, polka-dotted group launched from relative obscurity into the mainstream after a live performance recorded for KEXP went viral earlier this year, unexpectedly racking up tens of millions of views across the station’s social media platforms. They may not be Washington-reared, but the Emerald City can take a tiny bit of credit.
 Seattle’s classical music scene also made a strong showing. Dmitriy Lipay , the Seattle Symphony’s director of audio and recording, earned a nomination for classical producer of the year — the 20th nomination of his career, including eight wins. Among the recordings credited to Lipay are “Chen: Iris Dévoilée And L’Éloignement,” featuring the Seattle Symphony. Another project in Lipay’s portfolio, “Cipullo: The Dialogue of Memories,” features former Seattle Symphony associate conductor Alastair Willis, as well as Music of Remembrance, a Seattle chamber music and social justice nonprofit .
 In other home-state news, while she may not have Washington roots herself, Spanish singer-songwriter Rosalía has a notable local feature on her new album, “LUX.” The album picked up nine Grammy nominations, including best album of the year and best alternative music album, and features Yakima Valley’s own Yahritza y Su Esencia . The regional Mexican group collaborated with Rosalía on the track “La Perla,” which earned a nomination for best Latin song, proving that their blend of música mexicana and urban sierreño has made waves well beyond the valley.
 Olivia Petty is a Seattle-based freelancer and former features intern at The Seattle Times. She also previously interned at The San Diego Union-Tribune and served as editor-in-chief of Smith College’s student newspaper, The Sophian.
